aboutH2: Simon House Recovery Centre: Residential Treatment for Men in Calgary
intro: Simon House Recovery Centre is a rehabilitation treatment located in Alberta. It has three phases by which they accomplish the rehabilitation of male individuals. Phase one consists of a 12-week program, in which they go through intensive individual and group therapy session and also a recovery program to get over the drugs. Then if the addicts wish, they can go through phase two and three. Those consist of a transitional house and independent living. They provide ongoing support for the recovering addicts to make sure they truly make it. The point is to empower the men and to teach them abstinence from drugs.

Today the active treatment phase runs for 84 days, and Alberta residents pay nothing for it. The program is for men only, and every resident lives on site in Bowness, a riverside neighbourhood in northwest Calgary.

pillars.title: Three Buildings on Bowness Road in Northwest Calgary
pillars.body: Simon House started in 1982 in a Bowness duplex, and that duplex still houses men in the program. The house next door was donated a year later. In 2006 donors paid for a 30-bed building with a commercial kitchen, a boardroom and offices, and today the three buildings hold up to 67 men. Meals come out of that kitchen and are eaten together in a shared dining room. Bowness is a quiet residential area on the Bow River, and residents are free to leave the property when they are not in program, as long as they are back before the 11 p.m. curfew.

pillars.title: Free AfterCARE, Family Work and an Alumni Network
pillars.body: Graduates can join the AfterCARE program, which is free (donations are accepted). It offers individual and group mentorship, life coaching, family reunification and family conferencing, plus the alumni community that comes back every week to speak to men still in treatment. Before finishing, residents can also connect with an outside recovery coach through Recovery Coaches Alberta. Partnerships with Jewish Family Services Calgary and Alcove Calgary add counselling, housing help and family reunification support, and both are open to clients of any background.

pillars.title: Counsellors, Case Workers and an Indigenous Program Team
pillars.body: Dr. John Rook is President and CEO. The clinical side is led by Wade Cory, Director of Clinical Operations, with manager Holly Tait, three counsellors and four addictions case workers. A residential team covers the buildings around the clock. Wil Day Rider coordinates the First Nations program, and the centre keeps a full-time Indigenous Coordinator so that ceremony and one-on-one cultural support are part of daily life, open to every resident.

overviewH2: Simon House Recovery Centre: Center Overview
overview: Simon House is an abstinence-based residential program for men with drug or alcohol addiction. Men choose from four recovery pathways: the 12 Steps of AA and NA, Wellbriety, Recovery Dharma and SMART Recovery, which draws on CBT skills. Counselling is one-on-one and in groups, and men already on methadone or Suboxone can be admitted through the Medication Assisted Recovery program run with the AHS Opioid Dependency Program.

location.heading: Simon House Recovery Centre in Calgary, Alberta
location.intro: Simon House is on Bowness Road NW in Bowness, a northwest Calgary neighbourhood beside the Bow River, close to the Trans-Canada Highway and Stoney Trail. Downtown Calgary is about 20 minutes away by car, Cochrane about 25 minutes and Airdrie about half an hour, while Canmore is about an hour west through the foothills and Red Deer about an hour and three quarters north.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's listing and its own website. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: How much does Simon House cost?
faqs.a: There is no cost for treatment for Alberta residents. The centre says its 12-week program is fully funded with support from AHS, other grants, donations and fundraising, and that no man is turned away for lack of funds. You will want some spending money for your stay, and anyone from outside Alberta should ask admissions about fees.

faqs.q: How long is the program at Simon House?
faqs.a: Active treatment lasts 84 days, which is 12 weeks. It is a full-time residential program, so you cannot work while you are in it. After active treatment, graduates can move on to the free AfterCARE program.

faqs.q: Who can go to Simon House?
faqs.a: Simon House treats men with drug and alcohol addiction. Every client lives on site, because it is a residential program with no outpatient option. The centre takes men from across Canada, and Alberta residents are treated at no cost.

No, Simon House does not run a detox unit. You need 72 hours without mood-altering substances and a drug screen before you move in. The centre lists Renfrew Recovery Detoxification Centre in Calgary among its community partners, and men on methadone or Suboxone are accepted.

faqs.q: Do you accept methadone or Suboxone?
faqs.a: Yes. Men who are prescribed methadone or Suboxone are accepted through the centre's Medication Assisted Recovery program, which runs in partnership with the AHS Opioid Dependency Program. Your prescribed medications are reviewed when you arrive.

Usually there is, and its length changes all the time because Simon House admits men on an ongoing basis. Call (403) 247-2050 to ask where things stand. If there is no room, the centre can refer you to a certified recovery coach through Recovery Coaches Alberta while you wait.

faqs.q: Where is Simon House and how do I get there?
faqs.a: Simon House is at 5819 Bowness Road NW in Bowness, in northwest Calgary near the Bow River. It is about 20 minutes by car from downtown Calgary and about 25 minutes from Cochrane. Clients may not bring a personal vehicle, so plan for someone to drop you off.

You can join the free AfterCARE program, which offers individual and group mentorship, family reunification support, family conferencing, life coaching and an alumni network. Alumni also come back each week to speak at meetings, and graduates are invited to the monthly graduation meeting.

faqs.q: Can I use my health benefits or insurance?
faqs.a: For Alberta residents the program is free, so most men do not need insurance at all. The centre notes that many private insurers cover addiction treatment, so check with your provider if a fee applies to you.

faqs.q: Does Simon House have Indigenous programming?
faqs.a: Yes. A full-time Indigenous Coordinator works on staff, and residents can join sweats, daily smudge and meditation, Wellbriety, sharing circles and cultural events such as Pow Wows and Round Dances. The program is open to every resident, and one-on-one cultural and spiritual support is available.

faqs.q: Can I have visitors or keep my phone?
faqs.a: Yes, within set times. Visitors are welcome on weekdays from 7 to 10 p.m. and on weekends from 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. Phones go to the office at 11 p.m. and come back at 8 a.m. once chores are done.
